report:
### Conclusion
The claim that influenza vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease is **false**. Rigorous peer-reviewed medical research shows no evidence that flu shots cause or increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease. On the contrary, multiple large-scale studies demonstrate that getting an influenza vaccine is associated with a **reduced** risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.

### Evidence Overview
* **Origin of the Claim:** The myth originated in the late 1990s from unverified comments by Hugh Fudenberg, whose medical license was subsequently revoked. His assertions were never published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal and lacked valid empirical data (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._Hugh_Fudenberg).
* **Scientific Findings:** Medical organizations and researchers have thoroughly investigated this claim and found no supporting evidence (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot). A landmark 2022 cohort study published in the *Journal of Alzheimer's Disease* analyzed thousands of older adults and found that those who received at least one flu vaccine had a roughly 40% lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease over a four-year follow-up period compared to unvaccinated peers (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9484126/).
* **Broader Vaccination Research:** Further research from UTHealth Houston indicates that several routine adult vaccinations, including influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, correlate with a lower incidence of dementia (https://www.uth.edu/news/story/several-vaccines-associated-with-reduced-risk-of-alzheimers-disease-in-adults-65-and-older).

### Summary
There is no scientific basis for the claim that flu shots cause Alzheimer's disease. Medical consensus indicates that seasonal flu vaccination offers protection against influenza while simultaneously being correlated with a lower risk of cognitive decline.
